g.title: READ FAILURES. THEN GROUP THEM.
g.desc: Three conversation sheets become an expert note, then three red error categories with fictional counts 7, 5 and 3.
g.text: A label is useful when it points to a change.
Read new groups until the notes stop revealing new
failure patterns. Then check unseen cases.

g.title: WHEN DOES A FAILURE NEED A TEST?
g.desc: A decision tree branches from an important recurring failure into a code check or an interpretation-based judge.
g.text: The test should protect a real decision or behavior.
Is it important or likely to recur?
A simple fix can come first. Save the case so the same

g.title: ONE AVERAGE. TWO DIFFERENT STORIES.
g.desc: A 10 by 10 grid has 90 green shipping cases and 10 red technical failures; the aggregate hides 0 percent technical accuracy.
g.text: Measure the capability that your user needs.
The agent passes every shipping case and fails every
technical case. More shipping tests will not fix that.
Show counts and pass rates for each feature, condition and
risk. This grid is a fictional example.

g.title: THREE WAYS TO FOOL YOURSELF.
g.desc: Three paired red and green examples explain leakage, changing the evaluator and testing only easy cases.
g.text: A higher score does not always mean a better product.
× Prompt examples appear in the test.
✓ Split related cases together; keep a holdout.
× New prompt and new judge in one comparison.
✓ Freeze the judge while comparing the agent.
✓ Add hard passes, failures and ambiguous cases.
Record dataset, prompt, model, tool and judge versions

g.title: MATCH THE CHECK TO THE FAILURE.
g.desc: Four colored lanes distinguish code checks, model judges, preventive guardrails and domain expert review.
g.text: Is the rule disputed or changing?

g.title: ONE ERROR. ONE CLEAR VERDICT.
g.desc: A renter asks for free times; the agent creates a viewing without confirmation. A fail verdict points to step 2.
g.text: A specific rule makes disagreement easier to inspect.
Do not create a viewing before explicit confirmation.
What times are free on Thursday?
Step 2 creates a booking. The renter only
Return pass/fail + reason + evidence step. Keep tool/API
errors separate from a valid pass.

g.title: CHECK THE JUDGE AGAINST AN EXPERT.
g.desc: Confusion matrix: TP18, FP8, FN2, TN72. Failure recall 90%, precision 69%, specificity 90%.
g.text: Count false alarms and missed failures separately.
Tune on development cases; report on untouched cases.
These are fictional counts, not a universal target.

g.title: SAMPLE FOR WHAT YOU COULD MISS.
g.desc: Five sampling strata contain 24, 8, 6, 4 and 3 fictional review cases; risk sampling differs from production prevalence.
g.text: Review a few cases from each meaningful group.
Example review queue: 45 cases. Oversampling risk helps
discovery; it is not a traffic-weighted rate.
Mix random cases with targeted slices. Keep related
conversations in the same dataset split.

g.title: BUILD SYNTHETIC CASES WITH STRUCTURE.
g.desc: Three columns of features, personas and conditions combine into a renter case that needs prior listing history and a reference date.
g.text: Book viewing × returning renter × relative date
“Can I see the second flat two weeks from today?”
Include prior listings, today’s date and timezone.
Generate only plausible combinations. Verify the facts and

g.title: READ THE TRACE. NOT JUST THE ANSWER.
g.desc: A four-step trace correctly resolves listing and relative date, reads availability, then falsely claims a booking.
g.text: The tool result is evidence of what actually happened.
Today: 8 Nov · Europe/Chișinău. “The second flat” means
listing L-204 in the previous results.
“Can I see the second flat in two weeks?”
Start at the first unsupported action or claim. Here the
tool only read slots; the assistant invented a booking.

g.title: FIND THE STEP WHERE ERRORS COLLECT.
g.desc: Four transition bars use their own denominators: 2/40, 6/12, 1/18 and 3/5 failures. They do not represent unique conversations.
g.text: A transition view exposes a repeated weak point.
Inspect the date and escalation traces first. A hotspot tells
you where to look, not what caused the error.
Use one clear unit: transition attempts. Do not add these
counts and call them failed conversations.

g.title: KEEP EVALS IN THE RELEASE LOOP.
g.desc: Develop, release and operate form a loop: compare changes, enforce critical checks, sample traffic, and turn new failures into cases.
g.text: One saved failure should protect the next change.
Keep fixed failures and new regressions
Review drift, new errors, cost and
New failures → new cases → the next experiment
Version the evidence and rollback rule. A passing test set
is evidence for those cases, not a guarantee.
